I've been through many debates over this topic, as I'm sure many others here have as well, and I find that people that grew up with older games tend to go with gameplay, while people that started somewhat recently go for graphics. Then there are people like my sister that aren't too into games and prefer a more story driven experience as if they're watching a movie so they can really relax. I lean towards a heavy emphasis on gameplay but I also know that you need a balance of all three to really make an experience.
I know I don't speak for everyone, but that's just my experience with people that I know. A few of my friends will not even look at a game unless it's pretty and shiny, but they're also kind of PC snobs that drop several thousands of dollars every year for a new high end computer so that may skew some of the argument....

Gameplay, story, graphics, in that order. There are a few exceptions; story-driven games where the story takes precedence over the gameplay (like Planescape: Torment), but there are some games with a great story that I just can't play because of the gameplay (like Gothic). Then there are plenty of games with little or no story, but great gameplay, like most sandbox/crafting games. I can't think of any games with bad gameplay and story, but that look great that I've actually enjoyed.

Gameplay first and foremost. I can forgive no story and bad graphics if the game is fun to play. For example minecraft, bad graphics, no real story, but legos in a game world, very good game. Crysis 3, good graphics, bad story, bad gameplay. Bad game. Graphics in no way make the game, but it does add immersion, same could be said for storylimes as well.

Game play and a good story combined

Graphics are the least of my worries

Story to me matters the most, especially if its don't really really well but if the story is mediocre then good gameplay has to be present to make up for it otherwise its gonna be a drag to play

Gameplay by far.

Graphics are nice, but good aesthetics don't need high fidelity graphics. There are tons of games that tries to look hyper realistic for their time but look like absolute shit today, and there are tons of games that had a simple but appealing aesthetic that are truly timeless.

Story is good to have, but not unique to games. A good story doesn't need to be in a game to be a good story. Because of that a good story that is attached to a bad game is being held down, rather than the game elevated. The game needs to be as good as the story to give people real satisfaction in experiencing both at the same time.

It depends on the game, gameplay is a must need for actions games like saint row and battlefield. Story is more adventure type games like tele tele walking dead. Graphics are a middle ground they can make or break a game like last of us and journey it gave those games their true view and made them more amazing. Then you have games like the Order 1886 which looks great with ok controls and super super short( 3hr gameplay 2hr cut scenes)

There all equally important. I can't place one over the other. I'd much rather play a racing game like Mario kart 8 instead of a photo realistic racer like Forza, because the gameplay in MK8 is much better. However that doesn't mean I want to play a game with the graphics of the first Mario Kart if MK8 is an option. It's also why I'd much rather play a game like Halo over Call of Duty, graphically they are similar, although the art style is a bit different, but the story in Halo is far superior. I'd much rather have a balance of all three rather than a game that is far better in two of those aspects but ignores the remaining one. I feel many people also downplay Graphics alot lately, I dom't know if its a sense of being hipster or its the cool thing to say but I guarantee that nearly everyone now would much rather play a game of todays standards such as the witcher 3 how it is now than as an low res game from the 90s. I don't need 8k textures for a game to be good but graphics do help.
